scope: The geometry of parametric probability models and the optimizers built on it: the Fisher information metric and its variants (Fisher-Rao, Wasserstein), divergences such as the Bregman family and the dually flat structure they induce, steepest descent under a metric (natural gradient, mirror descent, Wasserstein natural gradient), practical approximations of the Fisher (K-FAC, damping, Fisher-vector products), KL-constrained policy updates seen as natural-gradient steps (natural policy gradient, TRPO), and spectral views of wide networks through the Fisher and the Neural Tangent Kernel. It deliberately leaves out the reinforcement-learning machinery that is not geometric (PPO clipping, advantage estimation, Atari and MuJoCo benchmarking), Lie groups and pose representations, equivariant vision networks, Riemannian motion policies for robot control, and robot-learning datasets and policies, which belong to other areas.

concepts.title: Natural gradient descent
concepts.definition: An optimization method that preconditions the loss gradient by the inverse of a Riemannian metric on parameter space, usually the Fisher information, so that each step follows steepest descent in the space of model distributions rather than in raw parameter coordinates.

near_pairs.name: Natural policy gradient
near_pairs.why: The same Fisher-preconditioned step applied to policy parameters; a reader may want it as a specialisation note rather than a separate concept.

near_pairs.name: Wasserstein natural gradient
near_pairs.why: Same steepest-descent construction with the Wasserstein metric in place of the Fisher-Rao metric; distinct metric, shared form.

near_pairs.name: Riemannian optimization
near_pairs.why: Natural gradient descent is recovered from Riemannian gradient descent with a first-order retraction of the exponential map (nielsen2018elementary-048, raskutti2013information-053).

near_pairs.name: Mirror descent
near_pairs.why: Mirror descent with a Bregman divergence is equivalent to natural gradient descent on the dual manifold (raskutti2013information-020).

concepts.title: Natural policy gradient
concepts.definition: A policy-gradient method for reinforcement learning that preconditions the policy gradient by the inverse Fisher information of the policy, taking natural-gradient steps with a chosen step size.

relations.quote: The natural policy gradient is obtained as a special case of the TRPO update

near_pairs.name: Trust region policy optimization
near_pairs.why: TRPO computes the same Fisher-preconditioned direction but enforces a KL constraint per update instead of a fixed step size (schulman2015trust-035).

near_pairs.name: Natural gradient descent
near_pairs.why: Natural policy gradient is natural gradient descent applied to a policy's parameters.

concepts.title: Wasserstein natural gradient
concepts.definition: A natural gradient in which the parameter-space metric is the pull-back of the Wasserstein-2 metric instead of the Fisher-Rao metric, so the update accounts for a ground metric on sample space and stays defined for models without a density.

near_pairs.name: Kernelized Wasserstein natural gradient (KWNG)
near_pairs.why: KWNG is an RKHS/Nyström estimator of the Wasserstein natural gradient (arbel2019kernelized-015), not the same object; could be its own method note.

near_pairs.name: Natural gradient descent
near_pairs.why: Same steepest-descent form under a different metric; li2018natural-021 frames it as replacing the KL constraint of the Fisher-Rao natural gradient.

concepts.title: Trust region policy optimization
concepts.definition: A policy-optimization algorithm that maximizes a surrogate advantage objective subject to a bound on the average KL divergence between old and new policies, solved with conjugate gradient on Fisher-vector products and a line search.

near_pairs.name: Natural policy gradient
near_pairs.why: Natural policy gradient is the special case of the TRPO update with a fixed step size instead of a KL constraint.

near_pairs.name: Proximal policy optimization
near_pairs.why: PPO is a first-order method designed to emulate TRPO's trust region (schulman2017proximal-004); a different algorithm, not in this packet's names.

concepts.title: Bregman divergence
concepts.definition: The divergence induced by a strictly convex, differentiable function as the gap between the function and its first-order Taylor approximation, which corresponds one-to-one with exponential families and induces a dually flat Hessian geometry.

near_pairs.name: Kullback-Leibler divergence
near_pairs.why: For exponential families the Bregman divergence of the log-normalizer coincides with a KL divergence (raskutti2013information-014, nielsen2018elementary-045); related, not identical.

concepts.title: Neural Tangent Kernel
concepts.definition: The kernel formed by inner products of a network's output gradients with respect to its parameters, which governs gradient-descent training dynamics in function space and becomes deterministic and constant during training in the infinite-width limit.

near_pairs.name: Fisher information matrix
near_pairs.why: The empirical FIM and the NTK share the same non-zero eigenvalues (karakida2019pathological-041); dual views of one Jacobian Gram structure, not the same object.

concepts.title: Fisher information matrix
concepts.definition: The expected outer product of log-likelihood gradients under a model's own distribution, which serves as the invariant Riemannian metric on a parametric family and as the curvature matrix that natural-gradient methods invert.

near_pairs.name: Empirical Fisher
near_pairs.why: Martens2014new uses 'empirical Fisher' for the training-target approximation, which is not the Fisher in general (martens2014new-025, -026); Karakida2019pathological uses 'empirical FIM' for the sample-averaged true FIM. Keep both out of this note's aliases.

near_pairs.name: Generalized Gauss-Newton matrix
near_pairs.why: Equals the Fisher when the output distribution is an exponential family in natural parameters (martens2014new-006), but is defined differently.

near_pairs.name: Neural Tangent Kernel
near_pairs.why: Shares the non-zero eigenvalues of the empirical FIM (karakida2019pathological-041).

concepts.title: Mirror descent
concepts.definition: A first-order optimization method that replaces the squared Euclidean proximity term of a gradient step with another proximity function, typically a Bregman divergence, and is equivalent to natural gradient descent on the dual manifold.

near_pairs.name: Natural gradient descent
near_pairs.why: Proven equivalent to natural gradient descent on the dual Riemannian manifold (raskutti2013information-020); different algorithm and coordinates, same trajectory.

concepts.title: Kronecker-factored approximate curvature
concepts.definition: An approximate natural-gradient optimizer for neural networks that models each layer's Fisher block as the Kronecker product of activation and back-propagated-derivative second-moment matrices, so the curvature can be inverted cheaply.

near_pairs.name: Natural gradient descent
near_pairs.why: K-FAC is an efficient approximation of natural gradient descent (martens2015optimizing-004, wu2017scalable-007); a relation of type 'approximates' has no slot in the allowed relation types.
